𝐑𝐨𝐥𝐞: Data Analyst (0–3 Years)
𝐈𝐟 𝐲𝐨𝐮'𝐫𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐚 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐀𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐲𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐢𝐞𝐰, 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧 𝐭𝐨 𝐠𝐨 𝐛𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐬𝐲𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐱 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐟𝐨𝐜𝐮𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥-𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝 𝐏𝐲𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐧 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠.
📌 These are actual Python questions asked by American Express — designed to test your logic, clarity, and business understanding:
🔹 Find duplicate rows using Pandas groupby() and filter()
🔹 Difference between merge(), join(), and concat() — with real-world dataframes
🔹 Fetch the 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝-𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐲 — nlargest() vs rank()
🔹 Employees earning more than their managers — self-merge logic with Pandas
🔹 Difference between apply(), map(), lambda, np.where() — and when to use what
🔹 Detect anomalies or fraud patterns using groupby().filter() and conditional logic
🔹 Reshape and pivot data — pivot(), pivot_table(), melt(), and stack()/unstack()
🔹 Working with datetime — parsing, extracting components, and time-based filtering
🔹 Year-over-Year or Month-over-Month growth — using shift() and pct_change()
🔹 Optimize Pandas performance — avoid loops, use vectorization and numba if needed
🔹 Real-world use of itertools, collections.Counter, defaultdict in data handling
💡 𝐓𝐢𝐩: Don’t just memorize Pandas functions — learn how to think in terms of DataFrames. AmEx wants you to write clean, readable logic — not hacky code.
